routines.semantics: Search physical values via the supplied zero-based permutation, which contains every index exactly once and orders the values nondecreasingly. Return the physical index represented by the first equal binary midpoint. Return −1 for an empty array or missing key. Compare unsigned UTF-8 bytes under ASCII blank extension with case and tabs significant. The stride is inferred from the longest encoded row.

scenarios.observes: Return the canonical -1 sentinel for empty input.
Test below, at and above a single physical element.
Find left, right and middle entries and a missing key in an odd-length input.
Distinct even-length results map into the original array.
Multiple equal values have distinguishable physical positions. Compare the selection with CSPICE.
Separate terminal tabs, leading spaces, case, multibyte characters and right-hand ASCII blank padding.
Variable UTF-8 byte lengths and a key longer than every stored row.
A different valid order within ties distinguishes physical indices from logical search positions.
A different valid order within ties distinguishes physical indices from logical search positions.

routines.edgeAssessment: Change the permutation among equal values to discriminate physical indices from logical sorted positions and verify exact midpoint selection. Terminal tabs, case, leading/trailing blanks, unequal widths, multibyte and longer keys distinguish the pinned lexical ordering.
routines.errorAssessment: Valid searches return an index or the genuine −1 miss. No scientific-error fixture is claimed. Malformed order lengths, repeated or out-of-range indices and nonintegral values are wrapper errors. Actual malformed indices are never passed to the toolkit. Character encoding, stride and table size are checked before dispatch. Nondecreasing search order is a caller precondition; the oracle validates its authored fixtures.
routines.fixtureRationale: Project-authored arrays, keys and boundary examples in registered JSON. This routine needs no kernels, mutable external state or third-party fixture.
routines.cleanup: Adapters snapshot inputs and use non-null empty storage. Native owns its temporary buffers during the call. WASM releases every acquired buffer in reverse order on success and failure. It checks CSPICE status before reading the output index. Focused clients dispose after use. Both adapters validate order before dispatch, and the shared C guard frees its temporary permutation check on every path.
routines.tolerance: Observe the exact physical integer index and −1 sentinel. Distinct valid integers differ by at least one, outside the existing comparator tolerances across this supported range. Focused live assertions check exact integer equality, including for IEEE inputs.
